subject: koala
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: koala gripping a eucalyptus branch stand.
Style: pixel art.
reasoning:
Looking at the render, the arms read as flat grey angular wedges instead of limbs hugging the trunk, and the depth placement seems off—the koala sits in front of the trunk rather than wrapped around it, so I need to rework the positioning so the torso overlaps the trunk correctly.

Checking the seating: feet rest on the branch and the torso bottom aligns with the branch top, so that part works fine. The floor shadow is just the backdrop tree leaves casting onto the ground, which is also fine.

The ears look good, but the crown tuft on the head reads as an odd flat slab rather than a tuft, especially in the three-quarter view, so I should reconsider that geometry.

Comparing head and body proportions, the sizing feels balanced, but the arm and leg sections look off — the box-section sweeps with smooth skinning create crumpled, wedge-like shapes at the shoulders and knees instead of clean limb forms. I think the fix is to swap these sweeps for chunkier, more rigid box-based limbs rather than smooth-skinned polyline sweeps.

For each limb segment I'll build individual frustum boxes per bone, connecting joints with small cube pieces to hide the gaps at elbows and knees, keeping everything square-edged for that blocky pixel look. I'm checking whether the pixel cell-paint shading will apply cleanly to these frustum box parts, and thinking through how the limb colors and shading will read once converted.

Now I'm positioning the arm joints — shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand — and planning to replace the sweep-based arm with a loop of frustum boxes along those points, adding small joint cubes at the shoulder and elbow for coverage. I also want to adjust the arm positioning so it hugs closer to the trunk, comparing the trunk's radius against the hand and finger placement to make sure nothing clips awkwardly.

I'm also noting that the trunk ends up mostly hidden behind the koala from the front view, and that the trunk's diameter looks too thin compared to the koala's body width — something worth thickening.

Now I'm working out the leg geometry, mapping the sweep points for hip, knee, ankle, and foot positions.

The feet end up partially embedded in the branch, which looks fine visually since the toes wrap over the top. Eyes, nose, and ears look proportioned well for a koala, and the leaf cards and twigs near the trunk top seem positioned correctly.

Checking the trunk and root flare — base sits at y=0.09, top at 1.06, resting properly on the turf at y=0.095. The koala ends up the tallest element in the scene at 1.23, and everything else lines up on the ground plane correctly.

The crown tuft reads a bit like a pale stepped slab, but the color contrast keeps it readable, so I'll leave it as is. I'm tempted to add extras like a gumnut cluster or more fur tufts, but I want to stay focused on the core fixes: limb positioning, shoulder-to-torso connection, and the eye size, since the eyes currently look too tiny against the dark fur patch. There's also a large black patch under the right arm I still need to check.

That dark triangular shadow near the arm sweep in three-quarter view is the arm shading causing the issue, so replacing that sweep should resolve it. The neck and jaw proportions between the head box and chest look fine as they are. Reconstructing the arm sweep points for the replacement...

Adjusting more joint segments...
